summary: A music play that never starts now reports a failure instead of leaving the room in silence until the audio controller is restarted.
details: The audio controller answered /music/play the instant a play was accepted — before ffmpeg was spawned — and several guards between that accept and the first byte of sound could then abandon the play with no event, no error and no state change. Found live 2026-09-21: two play_requested lines, no ffmpeg process in the container at all, zero follow-up events, and a room told 'Now playing' that heard nothing for 25 hours.

Every accepted play is now held to a start deadline. One that has produced no sound by then fails as start-timeout, which is a real stream-failed, so nora's bounded re-resolve retries the track and then advances instead of the queue dying quietly.
A play that arrives with no attached player fails as no-player and says so, rather than returning from the spawn path in silence.
A play deferred behind a speech queue that never drains is covered by the same deadline; previously it parked as the suspended slot forever.

The already-connected join path re-asserts the arbiter's player, which was only ever wired on a fresh join. Re-attaching the player it already holds is a no-op, so nothing that is playing is disturbed.
limitations: This makes the wedge visible and self-healing; it does not identify which of the three guards fired in the incident that prompted it, because the pre-restart state was not captured.
The speech queue is also drained rather than stranded when the player is gone, but no test covers that path: teardown clears the queue, so the state is unreachable in the current code.
